source: National Research Council 1997 Digital I&C Safety and Reliability Issues, mapped to current project

hazards.hazard: Required supervisory measurement becomes unavailable/invalid but automation continues using hidden true state.
hazards.source_theme: Ch.3 systems allocation; Ch.7 human-system information
hazards.evidence: M10.9.8.3 degraded measurement matrix; measured-state discipline
hazards.m11_action: Retain fail-closed tests and manual presentation checks.

hazards.hazard: UI presents model truth as though it were a measured instrument value.
hazards.evidence: Measured / Model Diagnostic / Unavailable provenance contracts

hazards.hazard: Stale measurement is syntactically valid but operationally too old for the decision using it.
hazards.source_theme: Appendix F timing and data consistency
hazards.evidence: Logical-step measurements; fault framework has unavailable/suspect cases but no general communication-age model
hazards.m11_action: No feature work; backlog explicit signal-age/delay modeling post-M11.

hazards.hazard: Requested SupervisoryAutomatic is mistaken for effective SupervisoryAutomatic while system has degraded to Assisted/hold.
hazards.evidence: Requested vs effective authority and degradation reason
hazards.m11_action: Keep persistent/visible distinction in final acceptance.

hazards.hazard: Training guidance mode changes physical control authority or controller behavior.
Manual takeover leaves supervisory automation still issuing new decisions, causing fighting controllers or mode confusion.
hazards.evidence: M10.9.8.3 takeover matrix and replay integrity

hazards.hazard: Normal/supervisory command bypasses, clears or outranks active protection.
Alarm ACK/RESET is confused with physical protection reset.
Duplicated software logic is described as independent/diverse although it shares the same functional requirement and failure-prone input space.
hazards.current_coverage: Avoided by architecture; no diversity claim
hazards.m11_action: Add non-claim; future diversity inventory post-M11 if needed.

hazards.hazard: Command appears accepted but no committed plant effect occurs and operator receives no clear observed-response evidence.
hazards.source_theme: Ch.7 strong/silent automation and control feedback

hazards.hazard: HMI availability/catalog is treated as final permissive authority and diverges from canonical runtime validation.
hazards.evidence: Contextual catalog explicitly advisory; runtime fail-closed

hazards.hazard: Keyhole effect forces operator to mentally integrate critical state scattered across pages.
hazards.release_disposition: Accept within declared HMI scope if persistent critical context remains visible
hazards.m11_action: Use checklist; no feature expansion in M11.

hazards.hazard: Clumsy automation reduces workload in easy conditions but increases operator burden during degraded/protection states.
hazards.evidence: Degradation reason, takeover, protection state; no formal workload study
hazards.m11_action: Representative degraded/takeover task in M11.6; deeper study post-M11.

hazards.hazard: Operator cannot tell which automation/controller mode is currently active or why it changed.
Dense alarms/events/mission data obscure the small set of safety-relevant changes requiring attention.
hazards.evidence: Alarm strip, first-out, bounded recent events, mission lifecycle spine
hazards.m11_action: Manual task/checklist; performance not visual redesign.

hazards.hazard: Automation acts correctly but is 'strong and silent': intent, inhibit, reason or result is not observable.
hazards.evidence: MODES state/reason, command observed response, LOG provenance

hazards.hazard: UI-thread work stalls long enough that operator-visible state/input becomes unacceptably delayed even though logical simulation remains correct.
hazards.evidence: M11.3 planned measurement; current serialized DispatcherTimer ownership

hazards.hazard: Catch-up/backlog policy silently skips deterministic simulation time to maintain wall-clock pace.
hazards.current_coverage: Current desktop path bounded without drop; generic API policy pending
hazards.m11_action: M11.3 supported-caller inventory and explicit policy.

hazards.hazard: Concurrent/mutable consumers observe different versions of plant/session state.
hazards.release_disposition: BLOCK if worker redesign weakens it
hazards.m11_action: Worker proposal requires immutable handoff contract.

hazards.hazard: Replay/checkpoint restores a state inconsistent with the exact scenario/action/authority history.
hazards.source_theme: Appendix F rollback/orphan-message analogy; Ch.4 configuration management

hazards.hazard: Historical fingerprint/schema/version is silently reinterpreted by a newer implementation.
hazards.evidence: Exact version IDs, fingerprint v1 anchor, schema v1

hazards.hazard: Recorder/evidence production fails but session is still presented as complete/authoritative.
hazards.source_theme: Ch.4 assurance; Appendix F information consistency
hazards.evidence: Current fail-closed evidence path; M11.3 planned failure-policy decision
hazards.release_disposition: Must be explicit before release claim
hazards.m11_action: Define compromised-recorder vs host-fault policy; never silent partial evidence.

hazards.hazard: Failed save destroys a previously valid session archive.
Runtime, manual, dependency versions, persisted formats and release statement describe different product configurations.
Runtime dependency update changes behavior or packaging requirements without corresponding release verification.
hazards.evidence: Central package versions and deterministic tests
hazards.m11_action: Freeze dependency matrix + clean-target publish tests.

hazards.hazard: Test-runner/tool change causes 'no tests executed' or coverage gaps to be mistaken for a green gate.
hazards.source_theme: Ch.4 product/process assurance; Ch.8 COTS role
hazards.m11_action: Gate must assert nonzero expected discovery/route resolution.

hazards.hazard: Project publishes invented numerical software reliability/safety probability unsupported by evidence.
